item.title: Are there ICE operations planned during Super Bowl LX?
item.description: Key U.S. Department of Homeland Security officials indicated in the fall that they planned to send agents to the Super Bowl.

item.title: Train derails in Mansfield; cars with liquid propane topple into river
item.description: The train had 43 cars; 14 derailed, including six carrying liquid propane. Four ended up partially in the Willimantic River.

item.title: Massachusetts, Nova Scotia announce partnership on offshore wind
item.description: The two governments will develop offshore wind in their respective areas and share knowledge, workforce, ports and, potentially, energy itself.

item.title: CT Rep.’s ‘ICE IN’ message draws rebuke from House speaker
item.description: House Speaker Matt Ritter dressed down lawmakers Thursday after a Bristol representative wore a message supporting ICE on her blazer.

item.title: Lamont kicks off universal breakfast push at West Hartford school
item.description: Gov. Ned Lamont's budget would allocate $12 million toward a universal school breakfast program; it's his second time pushing for the effort.

item.title: Hopes dim for quick resolution to Homeland Security funding bill
item.description: Negotiations devolved into a blame game among Republicans and Democrats over who should be talking to whom about the DHS funding bill.

item.title: CT legislature to weigh online safety, data protections for minors
item.description: Online privacy is a legislative priority this year, with several bills already introduced, including two put forward by Gov. Ned Lamont.

item.title: CT Siting Council rejects United Illuminating’s monopole appeal
item.description: Fairfield's fight against installing tall electrical transmission lines known as monopoles along MetroNorth rail may be over, for now.

item.title: A little flexibility gets Lamont a good start to election-year session
item.description: The fiscally cautious governor is signaling a willingness to compromise on spending and taxes, and Democrats are happy to see an opening.

item.title: The State of Housing in CT: Why it matters now
item.description: This report's findings point to a clear reality: Connecticut’s housing system is not meeting the needs of the people who live and work here.
